title: Silent Account Tampering and PII Exposure in a National Political Party Management System
summary: A self-initiated responsible disclosure engagement against a national-level political party management platform, uncovering unauthenticated password tampering, sensitive-data IDOR exposure, and session-lifecycle weaknesses.
industry: Government / Public Sector — Political Party Regulation

timeline.summary: Vulnerability discovered incidentally during normal use of the platform's registration flow.
Authentication, session, and membership-management flows reviewed using researcher-owned test accounts.
Findings triaged, severities assigned, secondary infrastructure observations scoped out of the core report.
Technical report and executive summary submitted to the platform operator.

confidentiality.summary: Sensitive personal data, including special-category fields, exposed to unauthenticated requests.

integrity.summary: Account credentials and party-membership records could be modified without owner consent.

availability.summary: No availability impact identified or tested.

privacy.summary: Ethnicity, religion, and contact data exposed via identifier-based lookups.

regulatory.summary: Exposure of special-category personal data raises data protection compliance considerations.

operational.summary: Silent credential tampering could erode user trust in platform account security if exploited at scale.

lessons.summary: Discovery-by-accident during ordinary product use is a legitimate and common entry point into responsible disclosure work — worth designing an intake process around rather than treating as an edge case.

Infrastructure-level recon findings (network devices, exposed management interfaces) warrant separate, more conservative handling than application-layer findings, and should not appear in public-facing material regardless of remediation status.
Coordinated disclosure with a defined escalation timeline (acknowledgment, follow-up, neutral third-party escalation) produces a clearer record than open-ended waiting.

seo.description: Case study on a coordinated responsible disclosure engagement against a national political party management platform, covering unauthenticated credential tampering, sensitive PII exposure via IDOR, and session-lifecycle findings.
